instruction: Could you please search for the paper 'World of Bits' on Google in Chrome?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('f11'); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5); pyautogui.scroll(-40)

metadata.explanation: Task requires extracting the main title 'World of Bits' from the PDF and searching for it on Google. The evaluator checks if the URL contains both 'google.com/search' and 'World+of+Bits'.
metadata.verification: Verified from PDF header that the paper title is 'World of Bits: An Open-Domain Platform for Web-Based Agents'. Task maintains similar difficulty by requiring title extraction and web search.

llm_judge_reasons: Semantic verification: Evaluator correctly verifies both requirements from instruction - 'search on Google' via 'google.com/search' pattern and 'search for World of Bits' via 'World+of+Bits' pattern
Coverage completeness: All instruction requirements are verified - no missing checks
Logical correctness: Metric chrome.py:70-99 uses regex search with AND logic, requiring ALL patterns to match (returns 1 only if all patterns found, 0 otherwise)
Data flow correctness: Getter chrome.py:710-800 extracts active tab URL from Chrome address bar via accessibility tree, which is the correct state to verify a Google search was performed
URL encoding handled correctly: 'World+of+Bits' matches Google's URL encoding of spaces in search queries
Practical feasibility: Postconfig includes 'wmctrl -a Google Chrome' to ensure Chrome is active before reading accessibility tree, no state timing issues
Pattern matching is appropriately flexible: Uses substring regex search, handles both http/https protocols
No semantic gaps: Instruction only requires Google search with specific query, which is fully and correctly verified by the evaluator
